title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 5 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: allies & theaters and drones & air autonomy.

stories.h: German Leopard tank in Ukraine survived 45 drone strikes
stories.what: A Ukrainian Leopard tank took 45 hits from FPV drones during Operation Vivaldi and is still operational, its brigade commander told military analyst Rob Lee. Lee, a senior fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute and a former U.S.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: The civilian office overseeing special operations forces could get $45 million budget, 100 staffers
stories.what: Hegseth’s proposed changes hinge on getting support from Congress.
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

stories.h: Germany plans 16 new A400M airlifters, a lifeline for the program
stories.what: Germany plans to buy 16 more Airbus A400M military transport aircraft, the German Defense Ministry said Friday, giving Airbus new work for a production line that has been running short of orders.
stories.you: Allies' wars and budgets are the testing ground and a big second market for new defense tech.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.h: GPS-denied navigation module ('Intel Inside' for drones)
idea.why: A small vision, inertial and terminal-guidance board any airframe maker can integrate; later, quantum-ready. Jamming is everywhere; most vendors can't build autonomy in-house. As airframes become commodities, the margin sits in components like this.
